## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Housing & Tenancy across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Housing & Tenancy Foundations & Core Mechanisms (Beginner / Scratch)** — Core physical and conceptual fundamentals, terminology, primary mechanisms, and foundational observation methods in Housing & Tenancy.
- **Tier 2: Housing & Tenancy Methodological Deep Dives & Empirical Evidence (Intermediate)** — Detailed instrumentation, measurement metrics, classification systems, and documented case studies of Housing & Tenancy.
- **Tier 3: Housing & Tenancy Advanced Systemic Paradigms & Comparative Dynamics (Upper Intermediate)** — Complex systemic interactions, historical shifts, anomalous patterns, and comparative analyses across different contexts in Housing & Tenancy.
- **Tier 4: Housing & Tenancy Frontier Technologies, Global Impact & Future Horizons (Advanced / Masterclass)** — Emerging technological breakthroughs, policy frameworks, environmental and human impact, and long-term evolutionary projections for Housing & Tenancy.

### Tier 1: Foundational Frameworks
1. **The Architecture of Housing & Tenancy: How Housing & Tenancy Developed**
   - *Question:* How did a city's rental rules develop alongside its housing market?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace one city's rental or tenancy system through dated housing policies and market conditions; distinguish legal changes from actual access. Evidence base: Trace dated origin records and subsequent interpretations. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf).    - *Question:* Which households benefited from a documented housing program?
   - *Key Focus:* Examine one housing program using eligibility, delivered units, affordability and tenure outcomes; identify which households the evaluation represents. Evidence base: Read the original evaluation and its population, comparator, outcomes and limitations. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf).    - *Question:* Whose tenant or maintenance work is missing from a housing-policy account?
   - *Key Focus:* Document overlooked tenant, maintenance or organizing work within one housing case; use consented accounts and avoid exposing vulnerable residents. Evidence base: Use attributable contribution records and consented participant accounts. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
4. **Housing & Tenancy: Understanding Housing & Tenancy**
   - *Question:* How do tenancy terms, deposits and repair responsibilities operate in one jurisdiction?
   - *Key Focus:* Explain rent, tenancy, deposits and housing quality through one jurisdiction's published rules and records; distinguish explanation from personal legal advice. Evidence base: Use primary definitions and a documented end-to-end example. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
5. **Housing & Tenancy: Tradeoffs in Housing & Tenancy**
   - *Question:* Why do affordability measures give different accounts of the same rental market?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare housing affordability measures using rent, income, household composition and unavoidable costs; explain why different measures yield different pictures. Evidence base: Compare original methods, assumptions, measures and uncertainty. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

Evidence base: Compare competing explanations and specify missing discriminating evidence. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf). Evidence base: Build a dated before-and-after record without assuming causation. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Starting framework: UN-Habitat housing approach evaluation (https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2023/12/global_report_evaluation_web.pdf). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

   - *Question:* Which costs and checks appear along a household's rental journey?

Evidence base: Trace the process, custody transfers and assigned responsibilities. Case records: local tenancy rules, housing inspections, household costs and documented program delivery. Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
